opportunities.title: Henry Moore Grants

amount.raw: New Projects and Commissions: max £20,000; Acquisitions and Collections: max £20,000; Conferences, Lectures and Publications: max £5,000; Long-Term Research: max £20,000; Research and Travel (individuals): max £2,500

opportunities.eligibility_summary: UK and international non-profit organisations (established and operating for at least 12 months) for New Projects and Commissions, Acquisitions and Collections, Conferences/Lectures/Publications, and Long-Term Research categories. Individual sculpture historians, academics and conservators can apply under the Research and Travel category. Applications from individuals wishing to develop their own artistic practice are not accepted.
opportunities.summary: Henry Moore Grants support the growth and development of sculpture across historical, modern and contemporary registers, funding exhibitions, exhibition catalogues, commissions, conferences, research, non-commercial publications, and development of collections (acquisitions, conservation, cataloguing, display). Applications are considered four times per year (Autumn, Winter, Spring, Summer rounds), each round open for one month.

opportunities.title: Visiting Research Fellowships

amount.raw: Expenses allocation: UK up to £600, Europe up to £700, Rest of world up to £1,000; accommodation provided for the duration of the fellowship. Senior Fellowships are six-week fellowships.

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Academics, curators, artists and researchers working on historic or contemporary sculpture. Research Fellowships at the Institute are for academics/curators; Artist Research Fellowships for artists developing their practice through research; Senior Fellowships for established scholars. Fellowships at Studios & Gardens are only for projects related to Henry Moore.
opportunities.summary: Fellowships allow researchers to spend a month using the Henry Moore Institute's research facilities in Leeds or Henry Moore Studios & Gardens in Hertfordshire, including accommodation, travel and subsistence expenses. Applications are currently closed for 2026/27; the next round opens in spring 2027.

opportunities.title: Dissertation Prize

amount.raw: BA dissertation: £250 cash prize; MA dissertation: £250 cash prize. Winners also receive Henry Moore Institute publications to the cover price value of £50.

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Open to BA and MA students of all disciplines whose dissertation was submitted within the past academic year at a UK university. Dissertations must relate directly to sculpture and not have been previously published.
opportunities.summary: Each year the Henry Moore Institute awards two prizes for outstanding extended pieces of writing on contemporary, modern or historical sculpture. Submissions for the 2026 prize will open in autumn.
